nahhas-irab:1-3.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). Some of the Arabs say «اللّذون» outside the Qur'an when it is in the position of a nominative.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is «قل أريتم من تدعون من دون الله», meaning with the nūn [i.e. «مَن» instead of «ما»]. «أريتم» is a well-known dialect form, widespread among the Arabs; «أرأيتم» is the original; and a third dialect form is to lighten the hamza after the rāʾ, making it "between-between" (bayna bayna, i.e. pronounced between hamza and the long vowel). Whoever reads «ما تدعون» uses it in its proper way, because it refers to the idols. Whoever reads «من» does so because they worshipped them, and so treated them as rational beings.
On this basis the readers agreed in reading خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ, and did not read «خلقن» or «خلقت», nor «لهنّ» or «لها».
ائْتُونِي بِكِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ هذا أَوْ أَثارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «أو أثرة». Al-Farrāʾ reported a third dialect form, namely (أثرة) with a fatḥa on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. أَثَرة as against al-Sulamī's form, which is presumably أَثْرة; the source prints them unvocalized], and al-Kisāʾī reported a fourth dialect form, namely «أو أثرة» with a ḍamma on the hamza [i.e. أُثْرة]. According to al-Farrāʾ the meaning in the three dialect forms is one, and the meaning, according to him, is "a remnant of knowledge". The meaning may also be, according to him, something transmitted (maʾthūr) from the books of the earlier peoples. So أثارة for him is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like al-samāḥa (generosity) and al-shajāʿa (courage), and أثرة for him has the meaning of athar (trace), as they say qatara and qatar, and أثرة is like khaṭfa. As for al-Kisāʾī, he said: athāra, athra and uthra — the Arabs say all of them, and the meaning in all of them, according to him, is one: in the sense of something transmitted (al-shayʾ al-maʾthūr). Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning of "the thing transmitted" is the thing that is related.
Among what has a sound chain of transmission from the Prophet ﷺ is that he heard ʿUmar saying "By my father!", and he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbids you to swear by your fathers; whoever swears, let him swear by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or keep silent." ʿUmar said: "After that I never swore by it, neither dhākiran nor āthiran." In one ḥadīth: "Whoever swears by other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has associated partners (ashraka)," and in another: "has disbelieved (kafara)." His saying «ذاكرا» means speaking it and saying it, as one says "I mentioned such-and-such to so-and-so"; and the meaning of «ولا أثرا» is: nor reporting about someone else that he swore by it. From this comes "a transmitted (maʾthūr) ḥadīth"; one says athara al-ḥadītha yaʾthuruhu (he transmitted the ḥadīth), and athira yafʿalu dhālika (he set about doing that), and āthara fulānun fulānan when he preferred him, and athāra al-turāba yuthīruhu (he stirred up the dust), and wathura al-shayʾu [ya]wthuru when it became soft; from this is said mīthara (a saddle cushion), in which the wāw changed into yāʾ.
Regarding the meaning of the Prophet's ﷺ saying, "Whoever swears by other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has associated partners," there are several views. The soundest of them is that the meaning is: he has associated something other than Allah with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in veneration, because a person swears only by what he venerates with the greatest veneration, and this ought not to be except for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Regarding his saying ﷺ, "has disbelieved," there are several views; among the soundest of them is that kufr is covering, and the meaning is: he has covered and concealed the veneration of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that ought to be shown.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ, i.e. who is further astray from the truth than one who calls, besides Allah, upon one who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection? Al-Farrāʾ said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «ما لا يستجيب له», and what is said about it is the same as what preceded.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: وَإِذا حُشِرَ النَّاسُ كانُوا لَهُمْ أَعْداءً, i.e. they will disown them and their worship.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِما تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: i.e. what you are engaged in. He said: from this comes "a ḥadīth mustafīḍ" and "mustafāḍ fīhi" when it spreads until people talk about it. كَفى بِهِ شَهِيداً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be accusative as specification (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)]. The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), brought for emphasis, because the meaning is "be content with Him". He said: when you say "kafā bi-Zaydin", its meaning is "kafā Zaydun" (Zayd suffices).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: قُلْ ما كُنْتُ بِدْعاً مِنَ الرُّسُلِ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-bidʿ and al-badīʿ mean the first. One says ibtadaʿa fulānun kadhā when he brings what did not exist before him, and so-and-so is a mubtadiʿ (innovator), from al-bidʿa, which is that for which no likeness preceded. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: بَدِيعُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ [al-Baqara: 117], i.e. their Originator. وَما أَدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلا بِكُمْ: the ḍamma has been dropped from the yāʾ [of أدري] because of its heaviness, and likewise وَإِنْ أَدْرِي.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ: it is said that شاهد has the meaning of "witnesses": a group of the Children of Israel who embraced Islam bear witness, on the basis that they had read the Torah, and in it is the announcement that the Qur'an would be sent down from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Among the most important of what has been narrated about this is what Mālik ibn Anas narrated from Abū al-Naḍr, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, who said: "I never heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ testify of anyone walking on the earth that he was among the people of Paradise except ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, and concerning him was revealed: وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Despite this, eminent scholars have contested this ḥadīth, among them Masrūq and al-Shaʿbī, who both said: It was not revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, because the sūra is Meccan and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām was in Medina; it was revealed only about someone else. Yet the ḥadīth has a sound chain of transmission, and against those who denied this it has been argued that the sūra, even if Meccan, may have had added to it some of what was revealed in Medina, because the arrangement is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He commands the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it as He wishes and wills. This is a clear view. It has also been said that Quraysh sent [people] from Mecca to Medina — because the scholars of the Jews were there — to ask about the affair of the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām testified to his prophethood ﷺ, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ — the verse. With all this, the ḥadīth, even though its chain is sound, it has been said that the words in it "and concerning him was revealed" are not the words of Saʿd, but rather the words of one of the transmitters, mixed into the ḥadīth without being separated.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كانَ خَيْراً ما سَبَقُونا إِلَيْهِ: Ibn al-Mubārak narrated from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: Some of the polytheists said, boasting, "We are such and we are such; if it were good, so-and-so and so-and-so would not have beaten us to it," meaning ʿAmmār, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and their like. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ [al-Baqara: 105].
وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا بِهِ: Sībawayh claimed that «إذ» is not used for conditional apodosis-taking (lā yujāzā bihā) until «ما» is joined to it, and likewise «حيث». Abū Jaʿfar said: The reason for that is that «ما» separates it from the verb after it, so it can govern it; when you do not bring «ما», it is connected to it, being muḍāf (in genitive construct) to it, and so it does not govern it. فَسَيَقُولُونَ هذا إِفْكٌ قَدِيمٌ, i.e. its like has come before in past ages.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
إِماماً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. one that is followed. وَرَحْمَةً is conjoined to إمام, i.e. and a blessing.
وَهذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِساناً عَرَبِيًّا: accusative as a ḥāl. One who is weak in Arabic imagines that it is a ḥāl from an indefinite noun, because what precedes it is indefinite; but a ḥāl from an indefinite is not good, and one does not interpret the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with something when something else is better than it. So لسانا is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (muḍmar) in مصدّق, and the pronoun is definite. Putting لسان in the accusative as a ḥāl is permissible because it has the meaning of "clear" (mubīn). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān used to say about this: it is a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl, and «عربيا» is the accusative ḥāl, as you say: "hādhā Zaydun rajulan ṣāliḥan" (this is Zayd, a righteous man).
«لتنذر الّذين ظلموا» with tāʾ — this is the reading of the Medinans; Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا. Abū ʿUbayd's choice is «لتنذر» with tāʾ, and he argued from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ [al-Raʿd: 7]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning in the two readings is one, and there is no choosing between them. Whoever reads «لينذر» makes it refer to the Qur'an or to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; if it refers to the Qur'an, the Prophet ﷺ is the one who warns by it, and likewise if it refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When the meaning is known, no choice arises in this, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَنْتَهُوا يُغْفَرْ لَهُمْ ما قَدْ سَلَفَ [al-Anfāl: 38]: it is known that the Forgiver is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the reading «نغفر» and «يغفر» are one; and likewise وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ [al-Baqara: 58] and «يغفر» are one, neither being more fitting than the other.
وَبُشْرى is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to «كتاب»; it may also be in the position of an accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)]. لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ: Ibn ʿUyayna said: iḥsān is generosity, justice and fairness.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا, i.e. upon obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then He, exalted be His praise, told what is theirs, saying: فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ, i.e. in the Hereafter, وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ over what they left behind in this world — so the people of exegesis said. After it is another khabar (predicate), namely أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ. خالِدِينَ فِيها: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ: a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ إِحْساناً: this is the reading of the Medinans and the Basrans, and likewise in their codices; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read إِحْساناً. [Translator's note: the source is evidently defective here: both readings are printed identically. In the transmitted readings the Medinans and Basrans read «حُسْنًا», while the Kufans (ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «إِحْسانًا»; what follows in the source assumes such a contrast.] It is narrated from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that he read «حَسَنًا» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the sīn. As for «حسنى» without tanwīn, it is not permissible in Arabic, because the Arabs do not pronounce forms like this except with alif and lām: al-fuḍlā and al-afḍal, al-ḥusnā and al-aḥsan. إحسان is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of aḥsana, and حُسْنًا has its meaning; and حَسَنًا is by putting the naʿt (adjective) in place of the noun it qualifies, i.e. "a good deed". The verse of Zuhayr is recited [metre: al-basīṭ]:
420- يطلب شأو امرأين قدّما حسنا ... فاقا الملوك وبذّا هذه السّوقا
(He seeks to reach the goal of two men who sent ahead good [deeds], who surpassed kings and outstripped these common folk.)
i.e. a good deed; and this is like this reading.
حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهاً وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهاً: this is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, and it is narrated from al-Ḥasan; Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ read «كَرْهًا» with fatḥa on the kāf. Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī opposed this reading with something which, if it were sound, would require avoiding it: he claimed that al-karh is anger and compulsion, and that al-kurh is the disliked thing [Translator's note: the source prints both words unvocalized; the vocalization given follows the sense of the argument], and he argued that everyone read لا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهاً [al-Nisāʾ: 19]. He mentioned that a certain scholar heard a man reading «حملته أمه كَرها ووضعته كَرها» and said: "If she had carried him under compulsion (karhan) she would have thrown him away" — meaning that al-karh is compulsion and anger. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this is an attack on those by whose reading authority is established; and his report from "a certain scholar" carries no authority, because he did not name him and he is not known — and even if he were known, his statement would not be authority except with evidence and proof. The authority in this is the statement of those who are known and followed: that al-karh and al-kurh are two dialect forms with one meaning. Indeed it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: al-karh is preferable, because it is the maṣdar itself. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them, reported that the maṣdar of every triliteral verb is faʿl, and they took as evidence for that that when you reduce it to the single occurrence (al-marra al-wāḥida) it comes with fatḥa, as in qāma qawmatan and dhahaba dhahbatan; so when you say dhahaba dhahāban, that for them is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), not a maṣdar. Likewise al-kurh is a noun of the maṣdar and al-karh is the maṣdar.
وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْراً: the implied form is "the time of his bearing", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Abū Rajāʾ and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصالُهُ, and it was narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan. [Translator's note: the variant reading is printed here identically to the received text; the reading attributed to these readers is «وَفَصْلُهُ».] Abū ʿUbayd argued for the first reading from the ḥadīth: "There is no suckling after weaning (fiṣāl)". Clearer than this argument is that fiṣāl is a maṣdar like qitāl, and this action is from two parties, because the woman and the child each separate from the other, so this is like qitāl — even though one may also say faṣalahu faṣlan and fiṣālan.
حَتَّى إِذا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ: according to Sībawayh it is the plural of shidda, like niʿma [and anʿum]. We have mentioned it in more detail than this.
إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the original is innanī; the nūn was dropped because of the accumulation of nūns.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: «أولئك الّذين يُتقبّل عنهم أحسنُ ما عملوا»: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ with nūn, and likewise «نتجاوز» with nūn, as statements from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about Himself; this reading was chosen only because of His saying وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ. The rest read «يُتقبّل» with yāʾ, and likewise «يُتجاوز», in the passive [and «أحسنُ» in the nominative]. وأَحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا: whoever reads with nūn puts أحسن in the accusative, because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)].

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
وَالَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "filth to you both". We have already mentioned the dialect forms of أفّ.
أَتَعِدانِنِي: some of the transmitters mentioned that Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym read أَتَعِدانِنِي with fatḥa on the first nūn; that is an error not known from Nāfiʿ — Nāfiʿ only gave fatḥa to the yāʾ, and it was wrongly attributed to him. Giving fatḥa to this nūn is a solecism (laḥn), and no attention is paid to what is recited [metre: al-rajaz]:
421- أعرف منها الأنف والعينانا
(I recognize of her the nose and the two eyes.)
I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: If something like this were permissible, there would be no difference between truth and falsehood; they abandon the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the eloquent dialects of the Arabs, and adduce as evidence a Bedouin who urinates [on his heels].
أَنْ أُخْرَجَ: al-Ḥasan read «أن أَخرُج», and its implied form is "that I shall come out of my grave". [Translator's note: the source prints al-Ḥasan's reading unvocalized; the active form is implied by the explanation.]
وَهُما يَسْتَغِيثانِ اللَّهَ, i.e. they ask Him and beseech Him to be gracious to them [both] with something by which he will believe.
وَيْلَكَ آمِنْ shows you that they argued with him and admonished him. ويلك is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
The one who said this imagined that, since the nations had not come out of their graves alive in this world, they would not be resurrected; that is his saying: وَقَدْ خَلَتِ الْقُرُونُ مِنْ قَبْلِي.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
أَذْهَبْتُمْ: this reading is narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «أذهبتم», and this reading is narrated from al-Ḥasan. [Translator's note: the source prints both readings identically; Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ's (Abū Jaʿfar's) reading is the interrogative «أَأَذْهَبْتُمْ», which the following discussion assumes.] According to al-Farrāʾ the two readings have one meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: The Arabs use the interrogative in rebuke and also do not use it; they say "dhahabta fa-faʿalta wa-faʿalta" (you went and did such and such) and they say "a-dhahabta fa-faʿalta wa-faʿalta" (did you go and do such and such?), and all is correct. [Translator's note: the source has «ولا نستفهم» "and we do not use the interrogative", most likely a misprint for «ولا تستفهم».]
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for what is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, it is the precise account of this: that, in his view, the correct course is to leave out the interrogative and read «أذهبتم», and in it is the meaning of rebuke, even though it is a statement. Its meaning, in his view, is: you exhausted your good things in your worldly life, so taste the punishment. The interrogative, if one reads «أذهبتم» [Translator's note: i.e. the interrogative form], is for rebuke and making them acknowledge (taqrīr). He chose «أذهبتم» without the interrogative only because when the interrogative carries the meaning of taqrīr it becomes a negation if [the statement] is affirmative, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ [al-Wāqiʿa: 58–59], and if it is a negation it becomes an affirmation, because the negation of a negation is an affirmation, as [the poet] said [metre: al-wāfir]:
422- ألستم خير من ركب المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطون راح
(Are you not the best of those who have ridden mounts, and the most generous in the world in the palms of [your] hands?)
However, whoever reads «أذهبتم» [with the interrogative] does not, in his view, take its meaning in this way; rather its implied form is: "Did you exhaust your good things in your worldly life and [yet] seek salvation in the Hereafter?"
فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ: the governor of اليوم is تجزون, intended as postponed [i.e. the adverb is fronted]. بِما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ, i.e. your arrogance and your transgression. When «ما» is a maṣdar-forming particle like this, it does not need a resumptive pronoun.

nahhas-irab:21-23.t:
وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ: عاد is fully declined (munṣarif) because it is the name of the tribe-as-people (al-ḥayy); if it were made a name of the tribe (al-qabīla) it would be a diptote, even though it has three letters. Likewise, if you named a woman Zayd it would be a diptote; and if you named her Hind, declining it fully would be permissible according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ — except that the preferred choice according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is not to decline it fully, while according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ full declension is better. As for Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj], he used to say: if you named a woman Hind, full declension is not permissible at all; and this is the analogical rule, because it is feminine and definite.
As for the statement of some grammarians that if you name [someone] with a past verb it is a diptote, Sībawayh refuted it from what was heard from the Arabs contrary to what he said, and [showed] that it has a counterpart among nouns; likewise one says "katabtu Abā Jādin" (I wrote Abū Jād) with full declension and nothing else.
إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ: Mujāhid said: al-Aḥqāf is a land. Ibn Abīn Nuʿaym said: al-Aḥqāf is the name of a land. [Translator's note: the name is so printed; it is probably a misprint, e.g. for Ibn Abī Najīḥ.] Wahb ibn Munabbih said: al-Aḥqāf in Yemen — the idols and the images, and they had overpowered people by their numbers and their strength. [Translator's note: this statement appears defective in the source; it is translated as written.] Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the singular of al-aḥqāf is ḥiqf, which is compacted sand, not very large, with a curve in it. He said: and one says iḥqawqafa al-shayʾu when the thing bends until its two ends almost meet, as [the poet] said [metre: al-rajaz]:
423- سماوة الهلال حتّى احقوقفا
(the outline of the crescent, until it curved.)
الأحقاف is fully declined, even though it is the name of a land, because it has alif and lām. Sībawayh said: Know that every diptote becomes fully declined when alif and lām enter it or it is made muḍāf (put in genitive construct).
وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ: plural of nadhīr, which is the messenger; النذر may also be a noun of the maṣdar. Al-Farrāʾ said: مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ: before him, وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ: after him. أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ: «أن» is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "bi-an" (that) [by removal of the preposition]. إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ: [عظيم is] a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم; if it were a naʿt of عذاب it would be accusative. Genitive by proximity (al-jiwār) is not permissible in the Book of Allah the Exalted; it occurs only in error.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عارِضاً has two answers. The implied form may be "when they saw the clouds", even though the clouds were not mentioned before, because the pronoun is known and «عارضا» indicates it. The other answer is that it is a reply to their saying فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا, i.e. when they saw what they were promised as a cloud. مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ: tanwīn is implied in it [i.e. the construct is not one of definiteness, so it can qualify the indefinite عارضا], and likewise قالُوا هذا عارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنا, i.e. «ممطر لنا» (raining upon us), as [the poet] said [metre: al-basīṭ]:
424- يا ربّ غابطنا لو كان يطلبكم
(Many a one who envies us, if he were seeking you…)
i.e. «غابط لنا».
بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: In the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: «قل بل ما استعجلتم به هي ريح فيها عذاب أليم». He said: هي and هو are like مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى [al-Qiyāma: 37] and «تُمنى» [Translator's note: the source prints «ويمنى» again; the variant reading is «تُمنى» with tāʾ]. Whoever says هو refers it to the punishment, and whoever says هي refers it to the wind.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: «فأصبحوا لا تَرى إلّا مساكنَهم»: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, and it is the known reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and of Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read فَأَصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ, and it is the known reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Mujāhid. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «فأصبحوا لا تُرى إلّا مساكنُهم» with tāʾ and with المساكن in the nominative as the noun of the passive verb [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. [Translator's note: the source prints the first and third readings unvocalized; the vocalization given follows the descriptions.] This reading is far-fetched according to al-Farrāʾ, because when a verb of a feminine noun comes first and is followed by an affirmation [with إلّا], the Arabs make it masculine, as he claimed, and he reported: "lam yaqum illā Hindun" (none stood except Hind), because the meaning according to him is "no one stood except Hind".

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيما إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «ما» has the meaning of "that which" (alladhī), and «إن» has the meaning of «ما» [i.e. negative], i.e. "We had established them in that in which We have not established you". وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ سَمْعاً وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً: hearing came in the singular and what follows it in the plural, and there is more than one answer for this. Among them: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and so was not pluralized for that reason; among them: that there is something omitted in it, i.e. "and We gave them possessors of hearing"; and among them: that it is a singular indicating a plural. فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ: «ما» may be a naʿt, having no position in i'rab [Translator's note: «نعتا» here is almost certainly a misprint for «نفيا», "a negation", which fits "having no position in i'rab" and the contrast with the interrogative]; if you make it interrogative, its position is accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ, i.e. returned [upon them]; he said: and the people of exegesis say: encompassed and befell.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنا ما حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْقُرى: this is the lām of emphasis. «قد» according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh has the meaning of expectation with the past; when it is with the imperfect it conveys the meaning of infrequency; you say "qad yaqūmu", i.e. that is infrequent from him.
فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْباناً آلِهَةً بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (28) فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ: لولا and هلّا (why not) are the same, as [the poet] said [metre: al-ṭawīl]:
425- بني ضوطرى لولا الكميّ المقنّعا
(O sons of Ḍawṭarā, why not [count] the armoured, helmeted warrior?)

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
i.e. هلّا (why not). قُرْباناً آلِهَةً: «قربانا» may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and may be a mafʿūl (object), with «آلهة» a badal (substitute) for it. بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ: if you wish, you may assimilate the lām into the ḍād. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh claimed that the ḍād comes out from the right side [of the tongue], and with some people from the left side.
وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ: «ذلك» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), «إفكهم» is its khabar (predicate), and the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of a genitive by being muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct); and its like is the same in i'rab and meaning [Translator's note: the source is elliptical here; it presumably refers to the variant «أَفْكُهُم», which al-Farrāʾ's remark then explains]. Al-Farrāʾ said: ifk and afk are like ḥidhr and ḥadhar, i.e. both have one meaning.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «أَفَكَهُم» as a past verb, the hāʾ and mīm on this reading being in the position of an accusative; there is doubt about its chain of transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās. However, it was read out to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, from Ḥammād ibn Salama, who said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, saying: I heard Abū ʿIyāḍ reading وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ [Translator's note: so printed, identical to the received text; given what follows, Abū ʿIyāḍ's reading was a past verb such as «أَفَكَهُم» or «أَفَّكَهُم»]. On this reading وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ is in the position of a nominative in one of two ways. Either it is conjoined to the pronoun latent in «أفكهم», the meaning being "and that ruined them and destroyed them — it and their fabrication" — except that conjoining to a nominative latent pronoun is far-fetched in Arabic unless it is emphasized or the speech is lengthened: if you said "qumtu wa-ʿAmrun" it would be ugly, until you say "qumtu anā wa-ʿAmrun" or "qumtu fī al-dāri wa-ʿAmrun". The second way is that «وما كانوا يفترون» is conjoined to ذلك, i.e. "that destroyed them and led them astray, and their fabrication too destroyed them and led them astray".
The clear reading, on which rests the authority of the community, is «وذلك إفكهم», i.e. "and that is their lie", and وما كانوا يفترون on this reading is conjoined to إفكهم, i.e. "and that is their lie and their fabrication". ما with the verb would be a maṣdar, and so does not need a resumptive pronoun, because it is a particle. If you make it mean "that which" (alladhī), a resumptive pronoun is inevitable, implied or overt, so the implied form would be "and that which they used to fabricate (yaftarūnahu)"; then the hāʾ is omitted, and its omission is good for several reasons: among them the length of the noun [i.e. the relative with its ṣila], that masculine is not confused with feminine, that it is the end of a verse, and that it is an attached pronoun. If it were detached, omission would be far-fetched — even though some have read تَماماً عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ [al-Anʿām: 154] [i.e. «أَحْسَنُ»] with the meaning "upon the one who is better", and some interpreted Sībawayh's statement «هذا باب علم ما الكلم» as meaning "which is al-kalim", and some narrated «هذا باب علمِ ما الكلمُ» without tanwīn on the basis that هو has likewise been omitted; and there is in it the far-fetchedness we mentioned. When it is attached, omission is good, as it has been read «وفيها ما تشتهي الأنفس» [al-Zukhruf: 71] and «تشتهيه». Abū Isḥāq reported «وذلك أأفكهم», i.e. "the most lying of them" [Translator's note: i.e. «آفَكُهُم», an elative].

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: وَإِذْ صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ: «إذ» is in the position of an accusative. It is said: the meaning of «صرفنا» is "We directed them (waffaqnāhum) to that", so it was called ṣarf (turning) figuratively. [Translator's note: the source reads «مضى صرفنا وقفناهم»; «مضى» is probably a misprint for «معنى», and «وقفناهم» may be for «وفّقناهم»; translated by the likely sense.] فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ, i.e. its recitation was finished, وَلَّوْا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ, i.e. warning them against refusing to accept the truth; «منذرين» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا كِتاباً: Sībawayh allowed, in some dialects, «أنّ» with fatḥa after a verb of saying. أُنْزِلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ: «يهدي» is in the position of an accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب; it may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is [itself] nominative because it is an imperfect verb.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: يا قَوْمَنا أَجِيبُوا داعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ: the apodosis (jawāb) of the imperative, and likewise وَيُجِرْكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ: this is not from fatigue; for fatigue one says aʿyā yuʿyī; and ʿayiya bi-l-amri yaʿyā and ʿayya bihi when he does not find his way to it.
«بقادر»: this is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «يقدر». [Translator's note: the source prints the first form as «بقدر», evidently for «بِقادِرٍ», the received reading which the following discussion assumes.] Some grammarians claimed that the reading «يقدر» is preferable because the bāʾ enters only in negation, and this is an affirmation, and expressed surprise at Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, how such a thing could have escaped them so that they erred in it, given their standing in Arabic. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this is an attack on those by whose reading authority is established. Moreover, the imams agreed in reading أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقادِرٍ [Yā Sīn: 81], and we know of no difference between the two, and the community does not agree on what is impermissible. The grammarians have spoken about the verse that perplexed the one who said this. Al-Kisāʾī said: the bāʾ entered only because of «لم»; this is a sound view, and I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān explain it clearly. He said: the bāʾ enters in negation, so you say "mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin" (Zayd is not standing); when the interrogative enters upon the negation, it does not change it from what it was, so you say "a-mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin", and likewise «بقادر», because before it is a particle of negation, namely «لم». Abū Isḥāq said: the bāʾ enters in negation and does not enter in affirmation: you say "ẓanantu Zaydan munṭaliqan" (I thought Zayd was leaving), and "ẓanantu Zaydan bi-munṭaliqin" is not permissible; if you bring a negation, you say "mā ẓanantu Zaydan bi-munṭaliqin"; and likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ, and the meaning is: "Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able, in their sight and in their knowledge?"
Abū Jaʿfar said: If someone says, "Why does the bāʾ occur in negation and not in affirmation?", the answer according to the Basrans is that it entered to emphasize the negation, because it may happen that the one addressed does not hear «ما» or imagines a mistake; when you bring the bāʾ, he knows that it is a negation. As for the statement of the Kufans: the bāʾ in negation corresponds to the lām in affirmation.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ: with the meaning "and remember a day".

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: بَلاغٌ: there are two views on its meaning. One is that it means "a little"; one says "he has no provisions except a balāgh", i.e. a little. The other view is that the meaning is "in what they have been admonished with there is a balāgh (sufficient communication)", as al-Akhfash said. Some said: al-balāgh is the Qur'an. It is nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is a balāgh"; whoever puts it in the accusative makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a naʿt (adjective) of ساعة. فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفاسِقُونَ, i.e. those who transgressed in this world. It is said that this verse is among the most hope-giving verses in the Qur'an, except that Ibn ʿAbbās said: the most hope-giving verse in the Qur'an is وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ [al-Raʿd: 6].
